summary: The non_gaia variant uses CrewAI as a declared framework but effectively does not use it — agents are plain Python classes, not CrewAI Agent subclasses, and the Crew object is created with an incompatible set of objects. The system addresses all functional requirements and has no critical security vulnerabilities, but contains a persistent domain mismatch (the entire system was built for rat detection, not cockroach detection), a dead analysis utility module that is never called, a duplicate data model, and continuous monitoring is absent. The overall structure is the cleanest of the three variants with clear file separation and working synchronous logic.

findings.description: The entire system was built around rat detection rather than the specified cockroach detection system. The main class is named RatDetectionSystem, data fields are named rat_count throughout, and alerts reference 'rats'. This is a fundamental mismatch with the stated requirements.
findings.evidence: main.py:12 'class RatDetectionSystem'; sensor_agent.py:7 'class SensorData(BaseModel): ... rat_count: int'; coordinator_agent.py:22 'print(f"Coordinator received data from {data.sensor_id} at {data.location}: {data.rat_count} rats")'.

findings.description: The code imports CrewAI and constructs a Crew object, but the agents passed to it (SensorAgent, CoordinatorAgent, AlertingAgent, NotificationAgent) are plain Python classes that do not inherit from crewai.Agent. CrewAI expects its own Agent instances with role, goal, and backstory attributes; the Crew is effectively inert and the framework provides no value.
findings.evidence: main.py:1 'from crewai import Crew, Agent, Task'; main.py:24-28 'self.crew = Crew(agents=[self.sensor1, self.coordinator, self.alerting, self.notification], tasks=[])' — none of those agent classes extend crewai.Agent.

findings.description: utils/analysis.py defines analyze_sensor_data() and identify_hotspots() functions that duplicate logic already present in CoordinatorAgent. These functions are never imported or called anywhere in the codebase.
findings.evidence: analysis.py:6-44 defines two standalone functions; grep of all .py files shows no 'from utils.analysis import' or 'analysis.analyze_sensor_data' call.

findings.description: SensorData is defined twice: once in sensor_agent.py (line 6, as a Pydantic model with rat_count: int) and again in data_models.py (line 6, also a Pydantic model with rat_count: int). main.py imports from data_models but sensor_agent.py defines its own, creating two independent schemas that can diverge silently.
findings.evidence: sensor_agent.py:6 'class SensorData(BaseModel): ...'; data_models.py:6 'class SensorData(BaseModel): ...'; main.py:6 'from utils.data_models import SensorData' while sensor_agent.py:6 declares its own.

findings.description: The system runs a fixed 5-iteration simulation and then exits. There is no continuous monitoring loop, which contradicts the requirement that sensors 'regularly transmit data to the central system or coordinating agent'.
findings.evidence: main.py:65-101 'def run_simulation: for i in range(5): ... time.sleep(1)' — terminates after 5 periods.

findings.description: CoordinatorAgent imports pydantic.BaseModel but never uses it; the class is a plain Python object and the import is unused.
findings.evidence: coordinator_agent.py:1 'from pydantic import BaseModel' — BaseModel is not referenced anywhere in the file.

findings.description: CoordinatorAgent.receive_data() stores the incoming data and returns it unchanged. No processing or transformation occurs inside the method; it acts as a passthrough, pushing the analysis responsibility entirely to post-processing methods called later.
findings.evidence: coordinator_agent.py:12-24 'def receive_data(self, data): self.sensor_data_history.append(data) ... return data'.

findings.description: Strength: Clean file separation — agents, utils, and data models are in their own modules with a clear directory layout, making the codebase navigable.
findings.evidence: Directory structure: agents/sensor_agent.py, agents/coordinator_agent.py, agents/alerting_agent.py, agents/notification_agent.py, utils/analysis.py, utils/data_models.py.

findings.description: Strength: Pydantic models in data_models.py (SensorData, AlertData, NotificationData) provide automatic type validation and clear schema documentation.
findings.evidence: data_models.py:6-22 — all three message types modelled as Pydantic BaseModel subclasses with typed fields.

missing_requirements: Ciągłe monitorowanie (continuous real-time monitoring) — the system runs exactly 5 polling cycles and exits rather than running indefinitely.
logical_inconsistencies: utils/analysis.py duplicates the hotspot and statistics logic from CoordinatorAgent.analyze_patterns() and CoordinatorAgent.identify_hotspots() but is never called, leaving two divergent codepaths that will produce different results if both are ever used.

The Crew object is constructed with custom agent objects but tasks=[] and no crewai.Task instances; CrewAI's orchestration machinery is never invoked, making the framework dependency a non-functional decoration.

SensorData is imported from data_models in main.py but sensor_agent.py defines its own SensorData class; the two classes are independent Pydantic models that share the same name but different import paths.
implementation_risks: CrewAI agent interface mismatch will raise AttributeError or TypeError if any CrewAI orchestration method is called on the custom agent objects.
The fixed 5-iteration loop means the system cannot be deployed as a real-time monitoring service without architectural changes.
Duplicate SensorData definitions will cause silent schema drift if one is updated without the other, potentially leading to runtime validation errors.
